text: Write an abstract class implementing an algorithm with one hole, and two subclasses filling it. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class Free    extends Account { Free(long s){super(s);}    long fee(long a) { return 0; } }
static class Percent extends Account { Percent(long s){super(s);} long fee(long a) { ___; } }
for (Account a : new Account[]{ new Free(1000), new Percent(1000) }) {
answer: balance += amount - fee(amount)|abstract long fee(long amount)|return a / 100
explanation: Verified: 1500 then 1495. `deposit` was written once; the 5 that `Percent` withheld came from a method the parent calls and does not implement. That shape is the template method, and its value is that the *order* lives in one place and a subclass cannot get it wrong because it never sees it. Chapter 26 shows the same structure with a functional parameter instead, needing no class at all.
